ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the figure that governs. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test; the trace reads 30.16 km against a booked optimal of 23.2 km, an excess of 6.96 km. That is 30.0% of optimal, so both establishment gates pass at once — above 20% of optimal and above 0.8 km in absolute terms.

Nothing impairs that measurement. The trace samples every 10 seconds at 100.0% coverage, has no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds, so none of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires. The deviation may therefore rest on the gps_trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

The rider's initial burden is discharged. POL-RD-08(a) is met because trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-03207 with the recorded pickup, start and end timestamps in sequence, and POL-RD-08(b) is met by the 6.96 km excess measured from an unimpaired trace, so the burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The rider carries no history that raises the corroboration bar POL-RD-08 sets: on the citable field rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d the figure is 0, so the 'excess below 30%' corroboration rule is not engaged on this claim.

The refund is then arithmetic, not discretionary. The trip is METERED and the multiplier is 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier. Charged total is 38.25. Recomputed against the booked optimal route: 3.80 base + 0.75 x 23.2 km + 0.28 x 31.3 min = 29.964, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no fixed surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo discount, giving a recomputed fare of 30.764. Charged less recomputed is 7.486, and the payable figure rounds UP to 7.50. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share of 38.25.

The driver's only answer is the chat line 'can we stop at Jurong Point first'. I do not dispute the message is on the record, but POL-RD-04 exonerates only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor' attributable to the instruction, and not one derived fact in this bundle identifies those leave and rejoin points or measures the distance between them. The only derived fact about the waypoint is proximity — the nearest fix is 49.5 m away — which shows the vehicle passed near Jurong Point and says nothing about how much of the 6.96 km that cost. The driver's counterparty statement cites no evidence ID and no clause, so under POL-RD-08 it is discarded, and even if his reference to the chat is read as pointing to EV-CHAT-03207, the exoneration remains unquantified on this record and cannot reduce the POL-RD-02 figure.

No external-cause explanation is available to displace the measured excess. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-03207-01, is MISSING — weight 0.0, no payload, no advisory covering the Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 corridor in this window — so no road-closure exoneration under POL-RD-03 can be run, and the driver has not asserted a traffic cause in any event. The excess stands as measured.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-03207-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: Nothing else moves the money: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and zero ERP, so there is no off-route pass-through correction to add or subtract under POL-RD-09, and the 7.50 refund computed under POL-RD-02 is the whole of the monetary movement on this trip.

The rider asked for this detour in the app. MSG-03207-001, sent by the RIDER at 11:55:13 — 60 seconds after the meter started at 11:54:13 — reads 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', and the driver agreed 20 seconds later. The instruction therefore comes from the rider, is timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor (no artifact places the corridor exit earlier; the requested waypoint was not reached until 12:14:03) and in any event falls well inside POL-RD-04(b)'s three-minute after-window, and it names a place specifically enough to act on. POL-RD-04(a) to (c) are met.

The corroboration POL-RD-04 demands is satisfied on the very field the clause names. chat_message.waypoint_hint for MSG-03207-001 resolves on the platform's own ingest to 1.237339, 103.736859 ('Jurong Point'), and the driver's trace passes 49.5 m from that point at 12:14:03 — well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m threshold, and the platform flags it within_threshold true. This is a field comparison, not an act of geocoding, and it succeeds.

Because the detour was rider-requested, the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, and materiality is assessed on the excess that REMAINS. The measured excess is 6.96 km, or 30.0% of the 23.2 km optimal; the POL-RD-01 establishment gate therefore requires more than 4.64 km remaining (20% of 23.2 km). The record identifies exactly one off-corridor destination — the rider's Jurong Point stop, which the trace confirms the vehicle actually reached — and no other cause of off-corridor travel appears anywhere in the bundle. Once that requested detour is excluded, no excess meeting the POL-RD-01 gate survives and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

The burden POL-RD-08 places on the driver is discharged, and discharged in the form that clause demands: a specific artifact and a specific clause. The artifact is EV-CHAT-03207, the chat log; the clause is POL-RD-04, rider-requested detour. The very artifact the rider needs in order to complain of the stop is the artifact that records the rider asking for it, and the driver's counterparty statement on file says the same thing.

POL-RD-14 does not defeat that reliance. That clause is confined to a rider instruction the trace does NOT corroborate — the vehicle never coming within 200 m of the waypoint. Here the trace comes within 49.5 m of the requested waypoint, inside POL-RD-04's 200 m threshold, so the instruction is corroborated, it is the cause of the measured off-corridor travel, and it is excluded under POL-RD-04 rather than set aside under POL-RD-14.

The trace this argument rests on is clean, so the corroboration drawn from it is reliable. It is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 237 fixes at a 10 second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. It is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no POL-GEN-02 discount attaches to it, and the 49.5 m waypoint approach computed from it is a real measurement rather than an artefact of a broken trace.

No repeat-deviation uplift applies on this trip. The deviation is established but not MATERIAL — 6.96 km is under the 8.0 km material threshold and 30.0% is under the 50% material threshold — so POL-RD-06 is not even engaged by this trip. Even if it were, the pattern test fails on the only fields the clause permits: deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 228 is 0.004, far below 0.05. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follows, and no other profile field may be used for that test.

There is nothing left for a pass-through correction to operate on. The fare ledger carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge: erp_gantries is empty, the off-route ERP total is 0.00 and the on-route ERP total is 0.00, and this trip neither originates at an airport nor carries a fixed surcharge line. No POL-RD-09 correction is due, and there is no billing-integrity defect to refer.

The chat log is complete and untruncated and contains exactly the two messages quoted above; nothing in it objects to the route at any point during the trip, and the friend named in the claim filed no statement in this bundle. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence id carries no weight, so a witness who is named but never recorded adds nothing to the rider's case.

NO_ACTION is the outcome that simply leaves the fare as the platform has already settled it: EV-FARE-03207 records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. On this rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION preserves that state, which is the correct result once the rider-requested detour is excluded — the rider pays for the trip the rider asked for.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — decision on dispute DSP-03207 (trip TRP-03207).

THE MEASUREMENT. The GPS trace EV-GPS-03207 measures 30.16 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off; the booked optimal route on the trip record (EV-TRIP-03207) is 23.2 km. The excess is 6.96 km, 30.0% of optimal — above both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km), so a route deviation is established, and I accept the rider's evidence on that point. The trace is clean: 237 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no POL-GEN-02 discount attaches, and it needs no independent corroboration.

WHY NO REFUND FOLLOWS. The rider's own in-app message, MSG-03207-001 (EV-CHAT-03207), sent at 11:55:13 — 60 seconds after the meter started at 11:54:13 and before the vehicle left the optimal corridor — reads 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', and the driver agreed at 11:55:33. Under POL-RD-04 the instruction (a) comes from the rider, (b) is timed before the corridor exit and in any event well inside the three-minute window, and (c) names a place specifically enough to act on — it is the clause's own example. The corroboration POL-RD-04 demands is satisfied on the field it names: the platform resolved the message's waypoint_hint to Jurong Point (1.237339, 103.736859) and the driver's trace passes 49.5 m from that point at 12:14:03, flagged within_threshold true and far inside the 200 m test. POL-RD-14 does not set that aside, because the trace corroborates the instruction rather than failing it.

WHAT IS EXCLUDED. POL-RD-04 excludes 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor'. On this bundle the Jurong Point stop is the only off-corridor excursion: the trace confirms the vehicle reached the waypoint, and nothing in the bundle shows any second excursion. The friend named in the claim filed no statement, and the claim's 'not a tour' cites no evidence id, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight. The measured excess is therefore the excess attributable to the one rider-requested detour; excluding it leaves nothing above the POL-RD-01 gate (20% of 23.2 km = 4.64 km) and no deviation survives.

THE 7.50 THE RIDER ASKED FOR. The rider's arithmetic — charged total 38.25 less a recomputed fare of 30.764, a refund of 7.50 — is correct in itself, but POL-RD-04 excuses the excess before POL-RD-02 runs: the rider asked for the stop, so the rider pays for the trip the rider asked for. The driver's submission that the whole excess is the requested detour is accepted; the rider's submission that the exoneration cannot be applied because no leave-and-rejoin distance is stated is rejected, because with a single requested off-corridor stop the measured excess is that distance. The driver's counterparty statement (which cites no evidence id and no clause) is not relied on; the finding rests on EV-CHAT-03207 and EV-GPS-03207.

NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires the rider to have been billed for less distance than the trace records, by more than 1.0 km. The fare ledger charged 30.2 km and the trace records 30.16 km, so there is no unbilled distance and nothing is owed to the driver.

NO REFERRAL. The deviation is not material (6.96 km is under the 8.0 km line and 30.0% is under 50%), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and in any event its pattern test fails on the only fields it permits — deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1 of 228 completed trips is 0.004 (below 0.05). No POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises: the fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and no surcharge (erp_gantries empty; off-route and on-route ERP both 0.00). The bundle's traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03207-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but no party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-13 are not in play.

RESULT. NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays 0.00. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. The monetary effect is nil, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05. If the rider can produce record-type evidence that the vehicle travelled off the optimal corridor somewhere other than the Jurong Point stop, that would reopen the attribution on appeal.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
